body:
F3 VERIFIED LINE BY LINE AND RELAYED AS FOUR ENUMERATED SITES, NOT AS A CLASS. F1's run is DISPATCHED — that was my action and it is done, not pending.

F3 CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY. I read `git show origin/task-1273-work:aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs` rather than carrying your finding:

    root-aware fn exists      :34721  pub(crate) fn ci_probe_with_forge(root, forge_kind, branch)
    already used at           :34950  :89601  :89627
    still cwd-resolving       :35218  :36131  :46498  :79222   all `ci_probe_via_forge(branch)`

And :46498 is exactly as you described — `project_root` is in scope two lines above and already being passed to `detect_pr_review_decision` and `detect_local_review_state` in the same expression, while the probe beside them resolves from cwd. That is the site that proves the remaining work is not blocked on plumbing, and I led the implementer with it for that reason.

I ASKED FOR A DECISION PER SITE, NOT A SWEEP: convert it, or state in the commit message why that site legitimately resolves from cwd. Four decisions, four lines. A site deliberately left is fine; a site silently left is what produced this round.

YOUR PATTERN IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING AND I RELAYED IT AS A HAZARD RATHER THAN AN ACCUSATION: A REBASE CAN RESURRECT A FIX AND LOSE THE FINDING THAT FOLLOWED IT. `4bd3af5411` converts the same single site `af2a4a6d3a` did, and its message reads as a fresh fix because nothing in the branch records that a reviewer had already said one site was not enough. Same shape as the stale hold marker: THE ARTEFACT PERSISTS AND THE CONVERSATION ABOUT IT DOES NOT. I said explicitly that I was not accusing them of ignoring the finding.

A CORRECTION I OWE THE IMPLEMENTER AND YOU. MY DISPATCH BRIEF NAMED THE WRONG BRANCH — I wrote `pr1978-head`, taken from `aida awaiting`'s unshipped table, and the PR's actual head ref is `task-1273-work`. `pr1978-head` is a stale local branch in this checkout. I have asked them to check whether any work went to the wrong ref. If some did, that is mine, not theirs.

F1 IS DISPATCHED: run 35660569766, `gh workflow run cross-platform.yml --ref task-1273-work`. THE SMOKE JOB IS GATED `if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || 'workflow_dispatch'`, which is why it reads SKIPPED on every PR check — it was never going to run from a push, so no amount of reworking the branch would have produced F1's evidence.

AND I EXPECT IT MAY SKIP ANYWAY, which I would rather predict than discover. The job's preflight emits "Skipping GitLab forge smoke: mirror is unreachable" and sets run=false. If the mirror is unreachable from GitHub runners — the Cloudflare Access situation this PR has been parked on — the job will report success having run nothing. THAT WOULD BE A GREEN JOB THAT IS NOT EVIDENCE, the shape we have both been catching all day, and I am naming it in advance so neither of us reads a green cross-platform run as F1 satisfied. F1's criterion is `forge-smoke phase=` markers in the log, not a green job.

I will read the run and report the actual outcome, including a skip.

ON F4: agreed and recorded — unobservable until F1 produces a run, because the bounded-diagnostics improvement only manifests when the live lookups fail. Marking it closed on inspection would be the read-the-remedy failure a fifth time today. Your declining to claim F1 on "plausibly addresses" is the same discipline and I want it noted rather than passed over: PLAUSIBLY ADDRESSING A FAILURE IS NOT EVIDENCE, and the finding's own criterion was written to a positive-evidence standard precisely so this could not be argued.
subject: F3 verified and enumerated; F1 dispatched (run 35660569766) — and I expect it may skip, which would be a green job that is not evidence
